## Review of part 2

Reviewer, 2026-11-24. Ran in a real browser (all passed): team-kept (34), team-page-kept (46), schedule-kept (59), schedule-grid, reschedule (15), draft-put-back (105); and a probe of my own (`.local/review-probe.mjs`, not committed), scripts on and off.

Kept safe: the notice is held per person per league (`accountId:leagueId`), the token's answer per person, league, token and every field, so nothing reaches another admin or league. Harmful text (quotes, `<b>`, `</form><script>`, 120 characters) typed in "Team details" comes back exactly, drawn as text, and nothing of it is in the address. A save draws a new token; a missing token only turns the guard off. The 14 browser tests changed from `?done=…` wait, ten seconds at most, for the "Saved" sentence that names the thing: none is weaker, several are stronger (`check-web-shell` now fails any 303 for a forged league).

- **Medium.** A team changed meanwhile is overwritten unseen (`teams-area/actions.ts` `answerTeamForm` with `list-forms/answer.ts` `refusedWith`). Open a team in two tabs, rename it in one, save other words in the second: refused, but `refresh()` redraws the page with the NEW version while the boxes keep what was typed, and the other person's name is shown nowhere. One more tap saves and wipes their change (probe: version 1 to 2, "Saved: the details of Mine on", the other's name gone). Builder three's "keeps the OLD version" is not so: it is the new one. Right: for a changed-since-read refusal, say beside each box the other person changed what is saved now ("Now saved: Meanwhile"), so the second save is made knowing it; a test in team-page-kept.
- **Medium.** No browser test proves the double tap on the team page. With `requestKeyOf` broken to always return undefined, team-kept and team-page-kept still pass (their `dblclick` is stopped by `useOneSubmit` with scripts on, and Chromium sends one post with scripts off); only `same-request.test.ts` and schedule-kept fail. Fix: in team-kept and team-page-kept, post the same form twice by request (as `check-web-shell` `post()` does) and count one team, one player.
- **Low.** A refused grid form still carries what was typed in the address (`schedule-builder/grid-answer.ts` `answerParams`, lines 118-162): a refused new round puts `label=Kept+%22secret%22…` in the address, so in the history, the server's log and the Referer. Only a round name, at most 120 characters, and a reload drops it (checked); but it is the one form left that does. Fix: hold a refusal's typed values in the one-time notice (or the same-request answer) and leave only `at=` and the anchor in the address.
- **Low.** The grid's fresh notice does not say which answer it is for (`perform-action.ts` line 60 leaves `thing: base`; `schedule-page.tsx` line 143 checks only `said`). Any fresh notice makes whatever answer words the drawn address holds be said: an older address reloaded in a second tab before the first tab's redirect lands says its old refusal. Fix: put a hash of the answer's query in `thing` and compare it.
- **Low.** Refusals are kept as answers for ten minutes too (`server/same-request.ts`). With scripts on a typing refusal does not redraw the form, so its token stays; tapping again unchanged after the cause was put right elsewhere ("not allowed", a season made meanwhile) gets the old refusal without trying. Fix: keep a refusal only a few seconds (a double tap's time), or not at all.

Broken by hand, then restored: `requestKeyOf` never keyed (caught by schedule-kept and the unit test, not by the team tests: above); `take` never clearing a notice (caught by team-kept, team-page-kept and schedule-kept, "a reload says nothing old").
